Interface BridgeDelegate

public interface BridgeDelegate
Interface implemented by the agent-classloader side of the bootstrap-to-agent classloader bridge.

Bridge pattern

BootstrapDispatcher is loaded into the bootstrap classloader so that ByteBuddy @Advice classes woven into JDK code can call it directly. However, the full chaos implementation (ChaosRuntime) lives in the agent classloader and is invisible to bootstrap code by name.

The bridge is crossed at runtime via a MethodHandle array: at agent startup, an implementation of this interface (ChaosBridge) is constructed in the agent classloader and its methods are resolved into unbound virtual handles against this interface. Those handles — plus the delegate instance itself, typed as Object — are handed to BootstrapDispatcher.install(Object, java.lang.invoke.MethodHandle[]), and each dispatch call supplies the delegate as the first argument so the bootstrap dispatcher can call through to agent code without any classloader visibility requirement.

Method mapping

Every method on this interface corresponds one-to-one with a public static dispatch method on BootstrapDispatcher and an integer handle-index constant (e.g. BootstrapDispatcher.DECORATE_EXECUTOR_RUNNABLE). The method signatures, semantics, and fallback contracts are identical to those documented on BootstrapDispatcher.

Thread safety

Implementations must be fully thread-safe. All methods may be called concurrently from multiple threads, including JDK internal threads that the agent does not control.

  • Method Details

    • decorateExecutorRunnable

      Runnable decorateExecutorRunnable(String operation, @Nullable Object executor, Runnable task) throws Throwable
      Gives the active chaos scenario an opportunity to wrap the submitted runnable before it is handed to the executor.
      Parameters:
      operation - a string tag identifying the submission call site (e.g. "execute", "submit"); never null
      executor - the Executor that will run the task; may be null when the calling context is not an executor subclass
      task - the runnable to potentially wrap; never null
      Returns:
      the (possibly wrapped) runnable; equals task when no active scenario applies
      Throws:
      Throwable - if the delegate throws

    • beforeThreadStart

      void beforeThreadStart(Thread thread, boolean poolWorker) throws Throwable
      Called immediately before Thread.start() transfers the thread to the OS scheduler.

      An active scenario may inject a delay, throw to block the start, or record the event for observability.

      Parameters:
      thread - the thread about to be started; never null
      poolWorker - whether a thread pool is starting one of its workers, which must not inherit the starter's session
      Throws:
      Throwable - if an active scenario injects an exception to suppress the start

    • beforeWorkerRun

      void beforeWorkerRun(Object executor, Thread worker, @Nullable Runnable task) throws Throwable
      Called at the top of a thread-pool worker's run loop, before the next task is dequeued.
      Parameters:
      executor - the thread pool owning this worker
      worker - the worker thread currently executing; never null
      task - the task about to run, when available from the framework; may be null
      Throws:
      Throwable - if an active scenario injects an exception to stall or disrupt the worker

    • decorateShutdownHook

      void decorateShutdownHook(@Nullable Thread hook) throws Throwable
      Evaluates a shutdown hook before it is registered with the JVM: a scenario can delay or reject the registration. The hook itself is registered: despite its name (kept with slot DECORATE_SHUTDOWN_HOOK, ADR 0001), nothing wraps it.
      Parameters:
      hook - the shutdown-hook thread submitted by the application, or null
      Throws:
      Throwable - if the delegate throws

      Called before CompletableFuture.cancel(boolean).

      Throwable - if the delegate throws
